content: Hello, first of all I'm new to programming and I'm learning, but I honestly liked your contribution, at first when I read I didn't understand anything, but when I read in the comments I saw that it was mentioned about prime factors of a number, I started to investigate and understood what it was about, and this knowledge is very useful, I started to do the solution and it was difficult for me to pass all the test cases but I did it, and I had to think a lot about optimization, it seems to me that this challenge helps a lot to learn and improve about optimization, For a clash of code it is difficult for those who do not know about this, which is why this would be more interesting for a puzzle with special emphasis on optimization.

❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: I don't like the 10^12 constraint for prime factorization using trial division. Either make it 2^32 and force the use of a more interesting implementation like a sieve, or make it something like 10^6 or 10^7 to make sure that all programming languages available can solve this by trial division (and players are certain that their language can solve this within the execution time limit)

I also think the problem description is unnecessarily long and complicated just to ask for the list of prime factors of an integer, which is a problem that everyone with a chance to solve this puzzle already knows about

❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: Tests and validators are not similar.

❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: In CodinGame, validators are hidden test cases used to verify that a solution works in all possible scenarios, not just the visible test cases provided in the problem. The key difference is that validators are similar but not identical to the test cases, ensuring that the solution isn't hardcoded specifically for the test cases. This helps to prevent players from tailoring their code to pass only the given test cases and ensures that their solutions are more general.

Validators balance the test cases by covering edge cases and different inputs, but they aren't revealed to players during the coding process. The goal is to encourage solutions that work under a wide variety of conditions, rather than ones that rely on specific test cases​.

After conducting research, I found a forum where developers and programmers discuss the many difficulties they face.

Please take this into consideration while approving:
https://www.codingame.com/forum/t/clashofcode-contributions/197199

In Test Cases:

The validators should be similar to the test cases but not identical.

As a python user, I cannot use the brute force method for this. My solution is:
n=int(input())
b=[]
i=2
while i**2<=n:
    while n%i==0:
        b.append(str(i))
        n//=i
    i+=1
if n!=1:b.append(str(n))
print(len(b))
print(" ".join(b))
This solution cuts off when i cannot be a factor of n. This one does work with the time limits, but requires a bit more knowledge about primes.
